record.paper_title: Discrepancy estimates for sequences: new results and open problems
record.original_question: Show that every two-dimensional digital sequence in base 2 has discrepancy at least c (log N)^2 / N for infinitely many N for some constant c>0, or at least establish this lower bound for a substantial subclass such as NUT sequences or finite-row sequences.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 17 Show that for all 2-dimensional digital sequences in base 2 we have DN ≥ c (log N)^2 / N for infinitely many N. Or, show this estimate at least for a certain class of such (low-discrepancy) sequences (e.g. for NUT sequences or finite-row sequences).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Fix the base $b=2$ and the field $\mathbb{F}_2$. A digital sequence in base $2$ in dimension $s=2$ is constructed as follows. Choose two infinite matrices $C_1,C_2 \in \mathbb{F}_2^{\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N}}$ (each column having only finitely many nonzero entries). For an integer $n\ge 0$ with binary expansion $n=\sum_{j\ge 0} n_j 2^j$, $n_j\in\{0,1\}$, write $\vec n=(n_0,n_1,\dots)^\top$. For $i\in\{1,2\}$ set $(y^{(i)}_{n,1},y^{(i)}_{n,2},\dots)^\top := C_i \vec n \pmod 2$, and define
$$x^{(i)}_n := \sum_{k\ge 1} y^{(i)}_{n,k}\, 2^{-k} \in [0,1).$$
The corresponding two-dimensional digital sequence is $\mathbf{x}_n=(x^{(1)}_n, x^{(2)}_n)$, $n=0,1,2,\dots$.

For $N\ge 1$, the star discrepancy of the first $N$ points is
$$D_N^* \;=\; \sup_{\mathbf{a}\in[0,1)^2} \left| \frac{1}{N}\#\{0\le n<N : \mathbf{x}_n\in [0,a_1)\times[0,a_2)\} \;-\; a_1 a_2 \right|.$$

A NUT (Niederreiter–upper-triangular) digital sequence is one where each generating matrix $C_i$ is upper triangular with nonzero diagonal. A finite-row digital sequence is one where each row of every $C_i$ contains only finitely many nonzero entries.

Problem. Prove that there exists an absolute constant $c>0$ such that for every two-dimensional digital sequence in base $2$,
$$D_N^* \;\ge\; c\,\frac{(\log N)^2}{N} \qquad \text{for infinitely many } N.$$
If a full proof is out of reach, establish the same lower bound for at least one substantial subclass of two-dimensional digital sequences in base $2$, such as the class of NUT sequences or the class of finite-row sequences.
artifact.status_search_result: Although Schmidt's classical lower bound $D_N^* \gg (\log N)/N$ holds for any one-dimensional infinite sequence and there are matching upper bounds of order $(\log N)^2/N$ for two-dimensional digital sequences (Faure, Sobol', Niederreiter), no general lower bound of order $(\log N)^2/N$ for the star discrepancy of two-dimensional digital sequences in base 2 (or even for the NUT or finite-row subclasses) appears in the available literature. Recent surveys and works on digital nets and sequences (e.g., Dick–Pillichshammer's monograph and subsequent papers) continue to list this as an open problem, with progress only on related $L_p$-discrepancy questions. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Discrepancy of Digital Sequences: New Results on a Classical QMC Topic
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of recent results on the discrepancy of digital sequences, listing open problems including matching lower bounds.
status_evidence.claim: The question of a general $(\log N)^2/N$ lower bound for 2D digital sequences in base 2 is presented as an open direction in surveys of digital sequences.

status_evidence.title: Digital Nets and Sequences: Discrepancy Theory and Quasi-Monte Carlo Integration
status_evidence.snippet: Standard reference on digital sequences; matching lower bounds for star discrepancy in dimension >=2 are noted as not established.
status_evidence.claim: No general $(\log N)^2/N$ star-discrepancy lower bound for 2D digital sequences is recorded in the standard reference.

status_evidence.title: Optimal L_p-discrepancy bounds for second order digital sequences
status_evidence.snippet: Optimal $L_p$-discrepancy lower-order matching results for digital sequences (different from star discrepancy).
status_evidence.claim: Recent progress addresses $L_p$-discrepancy, not the star-discrepancy lower bound asked here.
